message.subject: New number + adding my partner
message.body:
Hi,

Two bits of admin please.

1. New mobile. My old number went with my work phone. The new one is (0491) 573 087. If that doesn't answer, try the landline at home, 5550 3172 (Sydney number, no area code).

2. Can you add my partner kirra as someone who's allowed to talk to you about my account and deliveries? I'm on the road a lot for work and she's usually the one home to sign. Her mobile is (0491) 575 254 and her email is kirra.w at example dot com.

For the check, my last order is ORD-20020 (the replacement bottle, thanks for sorting that) and I was born 26/10/82.

Dan

policy.label: Policy P8.1: Account access, security and carers
policy.text:
Password resets. A reset link lasts 30 minutes, and a new link cancels any older one. If an email does not arrive, check spam, then check the email address on the account. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 30 minutes.

Login codes. Two-step codes are sent by SMS to the phone number on the account, and can be turned on under Security in the account. If codes do not arrive, support can switch codes to email after an identity check.

Identity check. Before changing an email address, phone number, delivery address or payment details, confirm two of: date of birth, postcode on file, and most recent order number. Never ask for a password or a full card number.

Carers and representatives. A carer or family member can act for a patient once the patient has listed them on the account with consent. We always accept information from anyone about a patient's health or safety, or a report that a patient has died, and act on it, but we do not share details or change the account for someone who is not listed.

policy.label: Policy P5.2: Failed payments
policy.text:
If a plan charge fails, we email the patient and try again 2 days and 5 days after the billing date. If the second retry fails, that month's order goes on hold with the reason "Payment failed" until a payment goes through. There are no late fees.

When a patient updates their card in their account, we retry within 1 hour, and a held order goes back to dispensing as soon as the payment succeeds. A failed payment is usually an expired card, a changed card number or a bank block; agents cannot see why a bank declined a charge, and should suggest checking the card details first, then the bank.

policy.label: Policy P5.4: Prices, price changes and concessions
policy.text:
Monthly plan prices. Australia: one product A$148, two products A$214; concession A$118 and A$171.

Price changes. We give at least 30 days' notice by email. A new price applies from the first billing date on or after the date it takes effect.

Concessions. About 20% off for holders of an Australian Pensioner Concession Card or Health Care Card, a New Zealand Community Services Card, or, in the UK, proof of a means-tested benefit such as Universal Credit. A concession is verified when it is added and re-verified every 12 months; we email a reminder 30 days before it is due. If it is not re-verified in time, the standard price applies from the next billing date, and the concession price returns from the next billing date after it is verified again. Patients re-verify by uploading their card or letter under Billing in their account. A new concession is added the same way, and the concession price applies from the next billing date after it is verified.

A change to the products on a plan changes the price from the next billing date. There is no referral programme and there are no discount codes.

policy.label: Policy P4.2: Late, lost, damaged or wrong orders
policy.text:
Late orders. 1 business day past the ETA: share the tracking and reassure the patient. 2 business days past the ETA: open a trace with Courierline, which takes up to 3 business days, and tell the patient we have done it. 5 business days past the ETA, or when Courierline confirms the parcel is lost: reship at no cost. Every reship of a prescription medicine needs pharmacist sign-off, usually the same business day, and is dispatched within 1 business day of sign-off.

Marked delivered but not received: ask the patient to check safe spots and with neighbours, and open a trace straight away. If the parcel is not found within 3 business days, reship at no cost.

Damaged or leaking: ask for a photo within 7 days of delivery and ask the patient not to use the damaged item. After pharmacist sign-off we reship at no cost. The damaged item does not need to come back; any pharmacy can dispose of it safely.

Wrong item: ask the patient not to use it. A pharmacist contacts them within 1 business day and the right item is reshipped at no cost.

Never promise a delivery date beyond the ETA shown on the order.

Hi [FIRST_NAME],

Thanks for sending both requests and your check details. Before we change a phone number on an account, we confirm two of your date of birth, postcode on file and most recent order number [3]. The team will use the order number and date of birth you sent to complete that check, then update your mobile number. Please note that login codes are sent by SMS to the phone number on the account [3], so this change will also make sure codes reach your new mobile.

For your partner, a family member can act for you once you have listed them on your account with your consent [3]. Until she is listed, we cannot share details with her or change the account for her [3]. The team will look into adding her and confirm with you once it is set up.

Kind regards,
[AGENT_NAME]
